phases.name: Make a parser fix reaching history visible

steps.name: Acceptance tests for the derived-changes report (RED)
criteria: The build's change summary distinguishes derived corrections from sighting bookkeeping, so a parser fix reaching history is visible rather than buried.

Sighting bookkeeping is the counters that move whenever an advert is re-seen: First Seen, Last Seen, Times Seen, Jobs Seen, Messages, Jobs Found. Every other harvester-owned column is a derived correction.
The changes summary goes to stderr, per DR-0004 rule 4; the existing plan/apply summary stays on stdout so --dry-run keeps printing its plan there.
--report <file> writes the detail: for every changed cell, its tab, key, column, and the value before and after.
--report is written for a real build and for --dry-run alike, because the plan carries the changes either way; a dry-run still writes no workbook.
A run with no derived corrections says so explicitly rather than printing an empty section.
plan.changes keeps its existing shape — the 9 merge-plan scenarios must stay green untouched.
The existing suite stays green: 22 files, 162 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.
steps.scenario_name: a parser correction is visible among the sighting bookkeeping
steps.implementation_notes: Implements DR-0004 (one owner per column) rule 4, which says: 'When a harvester-owned cell changes value between runs, record it. This is the signal that a parser improvement reached history — the payoff DR-0001 bought with the cache — and without a report it is invisible. Summary to stderr; detail to --report <file>.' The --report flag is already advertised in the CLI usage header but does nothing. Measured on the real corpus: of 58 reported changes in a run with resend overlap, 56 were First/Last/Times Seen and 2 were genuine derived corrections — so the signal DR-0004 rule 4 exists to surface is currently drowned about 28:1. Do NOT change plan.changes itself; the split is a reporting concern.

steps.name: Split the change summary and implement --report (GREEN)
criteria: The classification of bookkeeping columns is a pure function in src/core/; writing the report file is an adapter concern.
steps.scenario_name: a parser correction is visible among the sighting bookkeeping
steps.implementation_notes: See 01-01 and DR-0004 rule 4. Pure classification in core, file writing in an adapter, wiring in the CLI.
